learning_objective: 🎯 Master the structured art of expressing opinions, analyzing issues, and informing large audiences through formal article writing!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Articles are written to inform, persuade, entertain, or analyze a specific topic for a mass audience in newspapers, magazines, or blogs. The tone can range from highly formal to conversational.

A standard article has three main parts: 1. A catchy Heading + Byline (your name). 2. An Introduction that introduces the issue. 3. The Body (2-3 paragraphs) analyzing the causes/effects. 4. A Conclusion offering solutions or final thoughts.

Before writing, ask: Who will read this? An article for a school magazine about 'Exam Stress' will have a completely different vocabulary and tone than an article on 'Global Economics' for a national daily.

An informative article stays completely neutral, presenting all sides of an issue with facts. A persuasive article takes a strong stance, trying to convince the reader to agree with the writer's opinion.
Strong articles are backed by data. Using statistics, historical context, or expert quotes adds immense credibility to your writing and proves you know what you are talking about.

fun_activity.title: 👽 The Alien Explainer
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine an alien has just landed on Earth. Write a 3-paragraph article explaining the concept of 'Homework' to this alien. You must define what it is, explain why humans do it, and offer your personal opinion on whether it's useful!

exam_tips: 📌 Format carries marks! NEVER forget to write a bold, catchy Title followed by 'By [Your Name/Given Name]' right below it.
📌 Divide the body of your article logically. Use one paragraph for Causes, the next for Effects, and the final one for Solutions/Suggestions.
📌 End on a strong, forward-looking note. Use phrases like 'It is high time that...', or 'If we act now...'
quick_recap: ⭐ An article is meant to be read by the public, so clarity and structure are your best friends.
⭐ Always ensure your paragraphs transition smoothly using linking words like 'Furthermore', 'Consequently', or 'However'.
⭐ A well-chosen statistic in the introduction is one of the easiest ways to grab the examiner's attention.
